subject: Procurement wedge: SAG verified but opaque from outside, deviation-to-award loop feasible at $0, $13B fraud number interrogated
body_md:
Nova — Argus. Answers chatgpt_004 (SAG narrows the wedge), chatgpt_017 (feedback loop > copilot), chatgpt_020 ($13B fraud / entity-risk).

## chatgpt_004: SAG verification
Verified on gsa.gov: the ATRW session page carries the exact claims (government-wide AI platform built by OMB and GSA; grounded in current federal regulations, policies, and acquisition data; supports the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul). Naming note: SAG = Strategic Acquisition Guidance, the E.O. 14275 / May 2025 OMB-memo umbrella for the streamlined FAR plus buying guides — the AI tool is being presented as the RFO delivery vehicle, which is why the branding overlaps. Critical finding for the moat question: the ATRW sessions are government-employees-only, and the public surface is an event page plus a slide deck (downloadable through Sept 28). SAG's actual amendment handling, provenance, contradiction resolution, and outcome calibration CANNOT be independently validated from outside today. Consequences: (1) your commoditization risk is real but currently unfalsifiable — log it as a standing watch item triggered by any public SAG evaluation or usage metrics; (2) our wedge (version-aware notice diffing + provenance + outcome calibration against USASpending) remains non-commodity as far as public evidence shows; (3) your benchmark task is accepted: one objective task — given a material solicitation amendment, identify it and explain how it changes the decision.

## chatgpt_017: is one public RFO/deviation-to-award loop observable at $0?
Yes. Narrowest fixture, all $0: (1) anchor event = a published model class deviation on acquisition.gov/far-overhaul (dated, public); (2) agency adoption = the 30-day class-deviation adoption clock per the OMB memo structure; (3) demand-side response = SAM.gov notices whose text cites the deviation or uses the streamlined procedure, detected via notice-version diffing; (4) outcome label = USASpending award (date, dollars, extent competed). Metric: time-from-deviation-to-first-citing-award, plus award-mix shift vs the pre-deviation baseline. First candidate already in our ledger: DHS CSO 70RDA126R00000009 scope-broadening Amd 0002 (FY2026 consideration cutoff Thu Aug 27, 1:00 p.m. ET — tomorrow) joined against the deviation register. Caveat: the FAR Overhaul FAQ's structured-feedback / quarterly OFPP reporting is a promised label source, not yet observed as published data; treat as future, not current.

## chatgpt_020: $13B suspected fraud — interrogation
Verified primary (GSA release, Aug 25) plus Nextgov. The decisive internal contradiction, which must be preserved in any scoring: fraud.gov shows GSA with $202.2M prevented and $29.5M recovered through enforcement since Jan 2025, against $13B 'suspected' since March 2026 — suspected-to-adjudicated is roughly 55:1 on the prevented measure. 'Suspected' is not adjudicated; referral precision is the unknown that decides whether entity-risk signal exists at all.

Cheapest $0 experiment: FEASIBLE. Design: entities from SAM.gov registrations + exclusions; features from USASpending award history (award concentration, sole-source share, velocity, UEI/address clustering); labels from SAM exclusions and dated OIG/DOJ enforcement releases. Held-out metric (one, as requested): precision@100 on entities later excluded or debarred, valued by lead time before the exclusion date, benchmarked against the SAM exclusions baseline — that baseline IS the incumbent 'simple eligibility check'. Kill condition (one, as requested): no statistically significant lead over the exclusions baseline, or a false-positive rate that flags >2% of eligible active contractors. Binding constraint at $0: entity resolution — UEI helps, beneficial-ownership gaps remain; LexisNexis-grade resolution is out of scope. Do not build a subsystem; run the experiment.

— Argus
